en.name: Quinoa, uncooked
en.summary: Dry quinoa keeps about 2–3 years from purchase in a sealed container in a cool, dark cupboard. It is technically a seed rather than a cereal, and commercial quinoa has already been washed to remove its bitter saponin coating, which is worth knowing when you are judging a bitter taste.
en.pantry: An airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard gives 2–3 years from purchase. That is much longer than most whole grains manage, and it is a fair question why: quinoa's oil sits in a small germ within a hard, low-moisture seed, and the seeds are sold intact rather than cracked or rolled, so very little surface meets the air. Keep it away from the hob and out of the light all the same, and decant from the bag into a jar — bulk-bin quinoa is a common source of pantry moths.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for dry quinoa, and it does not need one: the cupboard figure already outlasts most kitchen stocks. In a very hot, humid climate an airtight jar in the fridge slows both damp and insects, but bring it back to room temperature before opening so condensation forms on the container and not on the seed. Cooked quinoa is a different food with a fridge window measured in days.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for dry quinoa. Freezing a sealed bag for a few days is a useful way to deal with moth eggs in a bulk purchase, but it is a pest measure rather than a shelf life, and a seed this stable gains nothing else from a freezer. Cooked quinoa, on the other hand, freezes very well and is the better use of the space.
spoilage: A bitter or paint-like smell from the germ oil turning.
A musty or damp smell, or seeds clumping together.
Webbing, larvae, small moths or fine dust in the jar.
A persistent bitter taste after cooking that rinsing does not remove.
tips: Decant into an airtight jar the day you buy it and date the lid.
Rinse before cooking if the pack does not say pre-washed; saponin is bitter.
Toast it dry in the pan before boiling for a better flavour.
Keep it out of the light — glass jars look good but sunlight does not help.

faq.q: How long does dry quinoa keep?
faq.a: About 2–3 years from purchase in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard.

faq.q: Why does quinoa keep longer than most whole grains?
faq.a: It is sold as an intact, hard, low-moisture seed with very little exposed surface, so its germ oil is much better protected.

faq.q: Why does my quinoa taste bitter?
faq.a: Usually saponin, the natural coating, if it was not pre-washed — rinse it. A bitterness that survives rinsing is rancid germ oil.

zh.name: 生藜麥
zh.summary: 乾的藜麥密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 2～3 年。嚴格說它是種子而不是穀類；市售藜麥通常已經水洗去除表面苦味的皂素，判斷「為什麼會苦」時這一點很重要。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算 2～3 年。這比大多數全穀長得多，原因也值得一問：藜麥的油脂集中在一顆堅硬、低含水量種子裡的小胚芽，而且它是以完整種子販售，不是壓碎或壓片，所以接觸空氣的面積非常小。即便如此，還是要遠離爐台、避免光照，並且從袋子倒進罐子——散裝藜麥是穀蛾常見的來源。
zh.fridge: 乾藜麥沒有公布的冷藏期限，也不需要：櫥櫃的數字已經比大多數家庭的庫存週轉長。在非常濕熱的氣候，密封罐放冰箱能同時延緩受潮與蟲害，但開封前先回到室溫，讓水氣凝在容器上而不是種子上。煮熟的藜麥則是另一種食物，冷藏期是以天計算的。
zh.freezer: 乾藜麥沒有給冷凍數字。把密封袋冷凍幾天，是處理大量採購時穀蛾卵的實用做法，但那是防蟲措施而不是保存期限；對這麼穩定的種子來說，冷凍庫給不了別的好處。反過來說，煮熟的藜麥非常耐凍，冷凍庫的空間留給它更划算。
spoilage: 聞到胚芽油變質後的苦味或油漆味。
罐內出現絲網、幼蟲、小蛾或細粉屑。
煮熟後持續發苦，而且沖洗也去不掉。
tips: 買回來當天倒進密封罐，並在蓋子上寫日期。
包裝沒寫「已水洗」就先沖洗；皂素是苦的。
下水煮之前先乾鍋烘一下，風味更好。
避免光照——玻璃罐好看，但陽光對它沒有好處。

faq.a: 密封罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 2～3 年。

faq.q: 藜麥為什麼比大多數全穀耐放？
faq.a: 因為它以完整、堅硬、低含水量的種子形式販售，暴露的表面極少，胚芽油受到的保護好得多。
如果不是預洗過的，通常是表面天然的皂素——沖洗即可。沖洗之後還苦，那就是胚芽油走了油耗。
